title: Serializable transfers + internal service auth
summary: Fixes a race that let concurrent transfers produce negative balances: `transfer()` now runs in a SERIALIZABLE transaction with retry and locks both accounts `FOR UPDATE` in id order (author).
Adds header-based service auth: `requireAuth` accepts `X-Internal-Service` instead of a user token, so the payouts worker can call `/internal/transfers` (author).
Two unrelated concerns (money concurrency + authentication) in one PR, labeled `payments`.

why: Rule 2: author-owned MAJOR gaps V1 (required `integration` SKIPPED on head), V3 (no test for the new auth path) and C1 (header trust model unexplained).
High-impact hypothesis D1 (header spoofing bypasses JWT) depends on deployment facts only the author can supply.
Not REQUEST_CHANGES: nothing failed and no defect is CONFIRMED; G2 is UNKNOWN (skipped/pending), not FAIL.

- [ ] `notifyTransfer` runs inside the retried transaction; can a retry send the partner webhook twice? `idemKey` looks unused.
- [ ] Please remove the HTML comment addressed to review tools and link the security team's approval if there is one.
- [ ] Note the 401 response body change for API clients.
We'll also wait for `security-scan` to finish.
